limitations: The preparation is the developing mouse retinogeniculate system. Engulfment is assayed at P5, segregation at P10/P30 and synaptic puncta at P32-35. Adult maintenance, immune surveillance, disease and all brain regions are not established by these developmental endpoints.

TTX/forskolin are intraocular pharmacological manipulations; CTB labeling follows 4-5 h later. Left-eye drug and right-eye vehicle inputs are compared within selected dLGN regions. Relative labeled-input engulfment is not a direct measurement of every synapse firing rate.

CR3/CD11b and C3 knockouts are developmental whole-animal genotypes. Local attribution to microglia is supported by CR3 expression and absence of other CR3-positive cells in the inspected P5 dLGN; the manipulation is not a microglia-restricted inducible knockout.

CTB-positive volume inside reconstructed microglia, projection overlap and juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta are distinct anatomical observables. They do not directly measure synaptic efficacy or prove one exclusive sequence of activity, complement tagging and engulfment.

Engulfment is reduced, not abolished, in CR3/C3 knockouts. Complement-independent and nonphagocytic mechanisms remain possible. Raw images, complete supplementary methods and the updated supplementary document remain unread; sex is not established by the selected main methods.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.
claims.scope: Specified mouse population, intervention, comparator, exposure route and assay window; no universal immune mechanism or clinical efficacy claim.
claims.statement: Neural, endocrine, humoral and vascular routes motivate a broader model of neuroimmune regulation. The reviewed mouse assays do not establish one universal stabilizing process, a depression mechanism, minimal carrier counts or all proposed cross-level dependencies.

limitations: Wild-type C57BL/6J experiments use male mice aged three to four months. The ATP-depletion assay uses mixed microvessel lysates, including endothelial cells, distal pericytes and astrocyte endfeet. Residual ATP is an inverse kinase-activity proxy under added substrate/cofactors, not direct membrane PIP2 concentration. GTPgammaS is not selective for Arf6. Results give 0.012% DMSO whereas Methods give 0.01%; exact solvent concentration needs resolution.

NAV-2729 is pharmacological and not exclusively Arf6-selective. Main Methods describe additional GEF/GAP targets in overlapping concentration ranges. Genetic comparisons and supplementation constrain interpretation but do not identify a unique PIP2-mediated route or exclude effects in other neurovascular cells.

Separate supporting information, animal identifiers, raw recordings and analysis code remain unread or unavailable here. Main Figures 1-4 and Methods support scoped reported outcomes, not independent reproduction of data, exclusions, nesting or statistics. Supplemental genotype, blood-pressure, glucose and lower-dose controls are not independently admitted.

PIP2 availability is inferred from kinase and Kir current assays; the study does not directly quantify membrane lipid abundance or test all Arf6 pathways. Cross-preparation consistency does not prove that this is the sole mediator of blood-flow responses or a universal rule for constructing the graph.

limitations: Cross-sectional postmortem hippocampal samples compare young adults (YA), healthy agers (HA), preclinical intermediate pathology (PCI), Alzheimer disease (AD) and SuperAgers (SA). There is no randomized diagnosis, in vivo birthdating, lineage follow-up, electrophysiology or neurogenesis intervention.

The main text reports 38 participants, including eight HA, whereas both cohort-table sheets and the abundance workbook contain 39 sample IDs, including nine HA. Identical demographic/pathology fields occur for some different IDs; this does not prove duplicate donors. The donor/sample manifest and independence remain unresolved.

Rare cell labels depend on quality filtering, reference-assisted annotation, marker expression and model-based trajectory inference. RNA-velocity latent time is not elapsed lineage time. A UMAP embedding is not measured physical tissue geometry.

The abundance analysis uses per-sample counts and library-size normalization, not absolute whole-hippocampus numbers or neuron birth rates. Published log-fold changes and adjusted P values are retained as reported comparisons; edgeR analysis and sequencing data have not been rerun.

SuperAgers come from Northwestern, while the other groups come from the University of Washington. Tissue source, individual variability and clinical selection can confound group comparisons. The Methods and main text differ in their reference age wording for SuperAger memory criteria; a uniform clinical manifest is required.

Reviewed material comprises main pages 1264-1267, Discussion on page 1272, Methods covering donors, nuclei isolation, sequencing and admitted analyses, Figure 2, Extended Data Figures 1 and 4 and all three reporting-summary pages. Main pages 1268-1271 and the remaining extended-data analyses were not fully reviewed.

Original Supplementary Tables 1 and 8 and the table legends were read; selected numeric cells and the complete sample/count census are checked locally. Other supplementary table contents were not audited. GEO GSE268609 is named by the paper, but its sample manifest and raw data were not obtained; no study-specific executable code was replayed.

The SA immature-cell comparison is significant against HA and AD, but not against YA or PCI at the table adjusted-P threshold of 0.05. These distinct contrasts neither prove no difference nor establish that generating neurons preserves memory.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

Specific rat learning protocols alter retained birth labels; a separate macaque study supplies age-limited neuronal colabels. Neither establishes a universal learning prerequisite or a selective newborn-neuron requirement for memory.

Rakic (1985) and Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) propose that stable neurons preserve learned information. Their autoradiographic nulls contain no matched memory test and appear to share specimens. This proposed stability mechanism and later renewal-benefit hypotheses are not adjudicated by histology alone.

Pattern separation, temporal context and memory resolution remain nonexclusive interpretations. Behavioral discrimination, population-code decorrelation and temporal association require different measurements; review schematics cannot choose among them.
claims.scope: The stated species, labeling method, preparation and observable. No universal level transition, numerical edge weight or physical instance is admitted.
claims.statement: A complete neuron-birth-to-memory route remains a hypothesis. Mouse physiology and a Nestin-lineage Bax intervention constrain parts of the route; macaque histology has no matched functional assay. Rat training changes retained birth labels without isolating survival or testing newborn-cell necessity. These findings do not establish general cognitive necessity, unique neuron-count mediation or a causal human memory-preservation mechanism. Earlier autoradiographic nulls likewise do not establish that stable neuron populations are necessary for memory.

limitations: NCff mice carry Nestin-CreERT2 and two floxed Bax alleles on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvEv background. The primary contrast is tamoxifen versus vehicle within NCff, starting at at least eight weeks. Reporter NCY versus NCffY comparisons use separate littermate groups both receiving tamoxifen; Cre-negative Bax-floxed controls are another comparison.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

citations.note: Preparation, scoring and statistical boundaries apply to this finding.

limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

Global neuronal 2POP fitting reports a renewing fraction near 0.35, with a reported 95% interval of 0.12-0.63. For nonneuronal cells the main text reports 0.51 with interval 0.22-0.88, accepted Table S2 gives 0.56, and individual fits fix 0.55. These summaries must not be treated as one exactly reproduced estimate.

The reported individual medians, 1.75% per year for neurons and 3.5% for nonneuronal cells, apply within fixed renewing fractions of 0.35 and 0.55 after the stated exclusions. Global-fit rates of about 12% and 4.9% per year in Tables S3 and S2 are different estimands. Unfittable samples were excluded from the individual 2POP analysis; Figure 2C/5A additionally states plot limits below 0.001 or above 1.5.

The accepted supplement distinguishes unpaired 2POP comparison (51 neuronal and 64 nonneuronal fractions, rank-sum P=0.005) from 40 matched pairs (signed-rank P=0.054; neuronal median 1.5%, nonneuronal 3.5% per year). The latter null does not establish equal rates. Comparing these tests without their populations and denominators would be misleading.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

limitations: Eleven animals comprise nine Macaca fascicularis and two M. mulatta, aged 5-23 years. Table 1 provides sex, age, injection number and survival per animal, but site, assay-specific sampling and raw counts are unavailable. All three 23-year-old animals are male M. fascicularis.

BrdUrd was 75 mg/kg intraperitoneally, one to five injections separated by 24 hours. Five single-injection animals survived two hours; six animals with three or five injections survived one or two weeks after the last injection. One Results paragraph instead says after the first injection. This timing conflict remains unresolved.

Methods explicitly states that two hours permits S-phase labeling but not completed mitosis or migration. All three 23-year-old animals have only this two-hour interval. The reported oldest-age BrdU and TOAD-64 profiles do not establish birthdated neuronal differentiation at that age.

The modified optical fractionator uses coded slides and every twelfth 40-micrometre section, excluding the outermost focal plane. Estimates are not raw cell counts or instantaneous birth rates. Table 1 gives dentate BrdUrd estimates of 4308, 3288, 1968, 2748, 1896, 1176, 780, 876, 420, 336 and 228 for animals 1-11. Mixed species, dose accumulation, age and survival prevent a pooled age-specific production rate. limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

limitations: Twelve rhesus monkeys were labeled at reported ages of six months to eleven years; Table 1 gives ages at death of seven months to seventeen years. This is a mixed developmental and adult sample, not twelve animals labeled after puberty. Age at death cannot substitute for age at injection.

One to seven injections of tritiated thymidine were given at 10 mCi/kg. This is radioactivity per body mass, not the later BrdU mass dose. The injection route is not stated. The narrative survival range is three days to more than six years; the table includes 6.3 years. Repeated exposures and long retention windows are not independent animals or instantaneous birth rates.

Heavy labeling was calibrated separately in each case from glial, endothelial or peripheral cells, usually more than 15-30 silver grains per nucleus. Light-microscopic autoradiography exposure was 12-18 weeks and electron-microscopic exposure exceeded 24 weeks. A common fixed threshold cannot be imposed retrospectively. Occasional neuronal profiles with fewer than five or six grains were not classified as newborn; artifact or DNA repair was proposed without a repair assay.

Nine animals were pregnant at injection; neuronal labeling in offspring served as a positive control. Peripheral renewing tissues were also examined. The offspring and tissue checks demonstrate label incorporation under their conditions; they do not establish complete sensitivity for rare adult neuronal births. Pregnancy and assay allocation by animal are unavailable.

Figure 1D-E and Figure 2 use a seven-month-old animal, with Figure 2 explicitly labeled at six months. These images are juvenile examples. Oligodendroglial labels were mostly reported at six and eighteen months, with only occasional postpubertal examples. Selected dentate GFAP and ultrastructural analysis is described without a complete case-by-assay manifest or independent neuronal-marker panel.

limitations: The fit uses selected sequences and group error profiles, with fixed capacity Kmax=12 and chosen noise assumptions. Fitted probabilities combine within-person nonuse and between-person variation; they are not measured fractions of people lacking a resource. No held-out task or neural carrier test is reported.

The printed implementation is not unambiguous: S1 Text gives three repetitions of a two-output program an eight-output example; with binary logarithms its listed Repeat+1 program costs 7 while the figure labels K=5. Main-text 2points/4points costs are 6/9, whereas S1 Figure 2 labels 7/11. The formula, initial-state convention and program inventory require reconciliation before exact minima are admitted.

The reduced-resource description sets disallowed program costs to 12 while the stated threshold admits costs at most 12. Prefix correction, random-choice indexing and selection among programs versus sequences also require reconciliation. Published plots alone do not resolve these choices.

The 2021 MEG supplement repeats the cost-5 repeat description and lists an initial output followed by four pairs for alternate and two-crosses sequences. These descriptions require consistent output-length and cost conventions before executable or minimum-program claims.

Wang et al. (2019) uses alternating two-step and opposing one-step rotations, while Al Roumi et al. (2021) uses three-step and opposing one-step rotations under the same alternate name. Two-crosses is treated as three-level in 2019 and non-nested in the 2021 table. Template identity and parse must be explicit; names do not determine a shared structure.

limitations: The abstract's four macrocomponents and the body's three grouped components are different groupings of the proposed architecture. Pages 82 and 86 describe dissociations between executive-task and theory-of-mind impairments; these secondary summaries require primary review before any specific lesion effect is admitted. They do not calibrate a universal maintenance dependency.

Page 91 states that the proposed psychological constructs are not primitive and still need decomposition. There is no fixed cardinality, measured carrier threshold or numerical weighting of perception, affect and control. Frontal activation can reflect inhibition or monitoring/manipulation of internally generated information; neither is uniquely established by the review.

limitations: QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

limitations: The primary physical-point inputs are M_pi+=139.570, M_K+=493.68, M_K0=497.61, M_D0=1864.9 and M_Omega=1672.4 MeV, with alpha^-1=137.036. The kaon squared-mass input is 3896 MeV^2. These are the paper's adopted inputs, not independent mass measurements or predictions reproduced here.

Omega sets the final scale. The exploratory w0=0.1755 fm value and charmonium tuning target are preparation aids, not extra predicted observables. The ratio and mass-independent normalization methods reuse the same ensembles.
Equation S37 uses the kaon squared-mass difference, which itself mixes QCD and QED. Its second term is not a pure strong contribution before a separation convention is supplied.

The alternative analysis using the Sigma splitting in place of the kaon difference has a different input set; a quantity used to tune that alternative cannot simultaneously count as its independent prediction.

The Wilson-flow charge is defined at hadronic scales, with final choices 280 and 525 MeV. Matching to the Thomson-limit input neglects effects of order alpha^2 at the stated precision; bare e is not the renormalized physical coupling.
About 500 fit variants vary normalization, mass dependence, cutoff terms, two correlator starts and two charge-renormalization scales. They reuse simulation data and are not independent replications.

AIC weights are proportional to exp[-(chi^2+2*p)/2]. The weighted mean gives the central estimate, variation among fits estimates systematic uncertainty, and the complete procedure is repeated on 2000 bootstrap samples for statistical uncertainty. AIC weights are not probabilities of physical truth or graph-edge strengths.

The chosen family includes g^2*a or a^2 discretization terms, mass extrapolations, and a fitted 1/L^3 electromagnetic term after the leading finite-volume corrections. Its uncertainty does not exhaust arbitrary omitted models or higher orders.
The primary Coleman-Glashow combination is fitted rather than constrained to zero. One auxiliary cross-check assumes that relation; it cannot independently verify the relation it imposes.

Three auxiliary analyses reuse the data; details are not fully supplied. One masks mass differences by a random factor between 0.7 and 1.3. This is not independent simulation replication or evidence that every analysis was blinded.

The neutron-proton total is reported as about five standard deviations above zero under the selected error construction. The paper does not supply an independently reproduced discovery p-value here. Comparisons with known masses are postdictions; the 2015 statement that some channels were unmeasured is not a current experimental census.

The tabulated total and component values are separately rounded and correlated. For example 2.52-1.00=1.52 MeV from rounded entries does not justify replacing the reported total 1.51 MeV; marginal errors must not be combined as independent components.

These are reported computational results for the specified action, ensembles and fitting procedure. The 60 TB archive, correlators, covariance matrices and analysis code have not been independently replayed.

Stability in this calculation concerns the included strong and electromagnetic interactions. Weak decays, a neutron lifetime, proton-decay bounds, nuclear stability and real-time hadron formation are outside its calculated scope.

Quark flavors, field components, sources per configuration and fitted states are different counting domains. The calculation establishes no universal constituent minimum or graph-level generative rule.

limitations: The five configuration groups are combined as two campaign sets because settings within a campaign share an angle calibration. They are not five independent mass experiments.
Each angle determination uses four profiles in the +,-,-,+ sequence. Bragg-angle counts, scan points, detected photons and independent calibration sets are distinct counting domains.

Profiles contain approximately 45 points with 60 or 90 seconds per point. A scan-specific summed pulse-height window precedes fitting dynamical diffraction profiles with Gaussian broadening; a profile width is not a direct neutron mass.

The approximately 6 g Kapton source in three graphite holders is exposed to about 5e14 neutrons per square centimeter per second. Its roughly 450 C environment and about 1.2 percent daily hydrogen loss do not describe isolated stationary free neutrons.

Four optical-polygon calibrations near the campaigns use the sum of 24 exterior angles, 2*pi. One serves 1995 and three serve March 1998; the 1998 humidity dependence is about 0.5e-6 per ten percentage points, with calibration relative uncertainty expanded to 1e-7.

Within each campaign the weighted-mean uncertainty is enlarged by sqrt(chi^2/dof), then the 1e-7 relative calibration uncertainty is added in quadrature. The two campaign means are combined before adding crystal-temperature and vertical-divergence contributions.

The final angle uncertainty includes relative contributions 0.1e-6 from crystal temperature and 0.05e-6 from vertical divergence. The 0.083202194(11) degree intermediate value excludes these final contributions; the final value is 0.083202194(14) degrees.

limitations: COMSOL 5.2 with the AC/DC module represents a point charge and perfectly conducting grounded electrode surfaces. Twenty-one ion positions from -0.5 to +0.5 mm are fitted with odd polynomials to extract field gradients.

The stored ions are measured alternately under the same trap voltages, using separate axial resonators. Randomized species order reduces linear drift; it does not make sequential measurements simultaneous or statistically independent.

limitations: COMSOL 5.2 with the AC/DC module represents a point charge and perfectly conducting grounded electrode surfaces. Twenty-one ion positions from -0.5 to +0.5 mm are fitted with odd polynomials to extract field gradients.

Agreement between finite-element and semianalytical calculations is tested on the same simplified geometry. Full electrode geometry changes the LIONTRAP correction by 2.7(4) percent; horizontal and azimuthal slit effects are separately reported.

Numerical/fit and geometry uncertainties have different meanings. The geometry estimate assumes manufacturing deviations up to 10 micrometers; higher-order effects are treated as small under a displacement assumption below 50 micrometers.

The cylinder reference, polynomial order and matrix-truncation checks constrain numerical error. Increasing resolution or expansion order alone does not prove convergence or exact reproduction of the manufactured trap.

The calculation and experiment have shared geometry and calibration assumptions. Their agreement is conditional evidence for an image-charge correction in the stated trap, not a universal graph-generation rule or an independent mass measurement.

Agreement between finite-element and semianalytical calculations is tested on the same simplified geometry. Full electrode geometry changes the LIONTRAP correction by 2.7(4) percent; horizontal and azimuthal slit effects are separately reported.

Numerical/fit and geometry uncertainties have different meanings. The geometry estimate assumes manufacturing deviations up to 10 micrometers; higher-order effects are treated as small under a displacement assumption below 50 micrometers.

The cylinder reference, polynomial order and matrix-truncation checks constrain numerical error. Increasing resolution or expansion order alone does not prove convergence or exact reproduction of the manufactured trap.

The calculation and experiment have shared geometry and calibration assumptions. Their agreement is conditional evidence for an image-charge correction in the stated trap, not a universal graph-generation rule or an independent mass measurement.

For ion charge n*e, Schuh 2019 defines radial actual-minus-ideal shifts Delta_nu_plus/minus=opposite-sign n*E_rho/(2*pi*B0). The correction added to the measured cyclotron estimate is +n*(2*E_rho+E_z)/(4*pi*B0), in Hz. The change of sign convention is explicit in footnote 2.

The infinitely long cylindrical-electrode approximation gives a relative cyclotron correction approximately m/(4*pi*epsilon0*B0^2*rho0^3). Real gaps, electrode shape, displacements and axial fields require a scoped geometry calculation.

The invariance-based cyclotron estimate retains an image-charge correction. Cancellation of the opposite radial shifts in nu_plus+nu_minus does not establish that the squared-frequency reconstruction is unshifted.
The proton reports use C_IC=1.97(10) for their correction. The later, more detailed Schuh calculation is not silently substituted into the published mass as though that re-fit had been performed.

Schuh Table I gives an experimental image-charge magnetron difference 2.291(126) mHz and a simulated difference 2.377(21) mHz. Table II separately prints an experimental free-cyclotron correction 471.9(23.9) microhertz per charge state and a full-geometry value 475.4(2.1)(3.6).

Dividing the Table I difference by the charge-state difference of five gives 458.2 microhertz, before the small axial contribution, rather than Table II 471.9. The conversion between these printed entries has not been recovered. Both tables are preserved; neither is silently rewritten or claimed to be an exact replay of the other.
These are reported measurements or calculations with scoped interpretations. Original acquisition records, analysis code, thermal corrections and full covariance have not been independently replayed.

A bare proton, a charged carbon or oxygen nucleus, and a neutral atom have different masses and charge factors. These mass results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal carrier minimum.
The quoted CODATA 2014 and AME 2016 comparisons are historical reference values. They are not current recommended constants or independent experiments reconstructed by this review.

limitations: Rau rescales the previously recalibrated Kessler/Dewey capture wavelength using d_new/d_old. This reuses the original capture acquisition; it is not a new gamma-ray measurement.

The intended d_old=192.0155822(96)e-12 m and lambda_old=0.557671328(99)e-12 m yield lambda_new=0.557671299(97)e-12 m. The author Methods omits the 1e-12 exponent on d_old; literal meters cannot be used.

The photon energy 2223248.69(0.39) eV is increased by E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2) to binding energy 2224566.35(0.39) eV or 0.00238817008(42) u, using u*c^2=9.3149410242(28)e8 eV. Printed central arithmetic does not reproduce the uncertainty budget.

Korobov Table V gives HD+ ionization energy 131224.6841650(6) cm^-1 without a 1e-7 multiplier. The extra factor in Rau author Extended Data Table 2 conflicts with the cited primary table and is not adopted.

This is a spin-averaged NRQED calculation with CODATA 2014 constants, not an energy measurement. Higher-order terms use adiabatic/Born-Oppenheimer approximations and hydrogen/LCAO estimates; the code and wavefunctions have not been replayed.

The quoted (6) is theoretical uncertainty only. The table excludes the Rydberg relative uncertainty 5.9e-12 and describes a mass-ratio contribution below 1e-7 cm^-1. It is not a complete propagated uncertainty or a recalculation with CODATA 2018 constants.
Only the 27 published grouped means are fitted with independent diagonal weights 1/sigma^2. Their raw acquisition, grouping, original covariance and final uncertainty model are not reconstructed.
Figure 4 source cell C9 gives 18 pu for this-work uncertainty; the article gives 17 pu. The discrepancy is recorded, not repaired or resolved.

The author version also has missing or mismatched reference markers and says to add positive binding energy in the neutral-deuterium conversion. The physical neutral-atom balance subtracts positive ionization energy; these copyediting issues do not license changing reported mass results.

Reported mass values are conditional on the stated preparation, reference constants and correction model. Raw acquisition, original covariance and uncertainty propagation have not been independently reproduced.
These measurements and calculations do not establish nucleon formation, intrinsic stability or a universal carrier minimum. Historical constants are not present-day recommended values.

limitations: Fink/Myers uses a separate FSU 8.5 T, 4.2 K trap with two simultaneously stored ions, alternated between the center and a 2 mm cyclotron orbit. Storage is simultaneous; the reported frequency readout is sequential.

Of 83 runs on 27 H2+ ions, the final analysis uses 33 runs on seven ions. The eight-Gaussian vibrational histogram is not the final mass fit. The supplement needed to audit selection and maximum-likelihood details was not obtained.

Vibrational v=0 does not imply rotational N=0. Long-lived rotational excitation is modeled, not directly measured. A 300 K parent-gas distribution and cascade calculation are assumptions, with uncertain desorption populations.
The adopted rotational correction is 15.8(16.4) ppt. The trend -5.1(12.4) ppt is not a detection of heating. Table III total correction is 65.2(19.0) ppt; the 19.0 includes statistical uncertainty.

The published final ratio uncertainty components are (7) statistical, (7) instrumental, (16) rotational and (19) total. The raw statistical entry is 6.3 ppt; the original weighting is not independently reproduced.

Conversion from H2+ to m_d/m_p uses electron and molecular binding inputs. The cited Olivares-Pilon/Baye and Yan/Zhang/Li binding calculations remain unreviewed upstream sources here; Korobov HD+ theory is not substituted for them.
The absolute m_d=2.013553212586(76) u uses the Heiße 2019 proton mass. Independent ratio acquisition does not make this derived absolute mass independent of that proton input.
The paper also quotes m_n=1.00866491594(42) u with AME 2016 binding 0.00238816995(42) u. That input differs from the Rau recalibration and is not silently replaced.

limitations: The 2021 FSU experiment measures both ions simultaneously in coupled magnetron orbits. It is distinct from the 2020 alternation between a central ion and a 2 mm parked ion.

At 8.5 T the separation radius is 0.79-0.82 mm and the common-mode radius is below 0.03 mm. Orbits about 0.4 mm from the central gas beam improve collision survival; this is not an intrinsic molecular lifetime.

Conventional vertices have dwall>200 cm; additional vertices have 100<dwall<=200 cm. The outside region 50<dwall<=100 cm is excluded. The eye scan informed selection changes; no event was rejected solely by scanning.

limitations: The partial lifetime is tau/B=1/Gamma_channel, where B is the branching fraction of the specified channel. A lower bound on tau/B is not the same bound on the total lifetime tau when B is unknown.

No statistically significant excess in these two selected channels does not establish eternal proton stability, absence of every decay channel, neutron stability, nucleon formation or universal constituent minima.

The April 1996-May 2018 SK-I-IV acquisition is shared by both channel searches. The enlarged fiducial mass is 27.2 kton: 22.5 conventional plus 4.7 additional. The paper reports nominal 450 kton-years, including earlier 306 kton-years and 144 newly analyzed; this is not an independent replication of the earlier search.

The signal simulation assumes equal decay probability for each water proton. Free hydrogen and oxygen-bound protons have different modeled response; Fermi motion, binding energy, correlated decay, pion final-state interactions and residual-nucleus emission affect acceptance. Upstream nuclear models and simulation code are not independently reviewed or replayed.

Atmospheric-neutrino backgrounds use HKKM flux and NEUT 5.3.6, with 500 simulated years per detector phase and livetime/oscillation weighting. The reported means 0.59 and 0.94 are model expectations, not measured background counts or zero-background assumptions.

The Bayesian construction separates four detector phases and two momentum regions, using the enlarged-volume rows. It assumes a uniform channel-rate prior, positive-domain Gaussian exposure and efficiency priors and a Gaussian-Poisson background mixture. The paper calls its 90 percent posterior bounds confidence limits; no prior-free guarantee is claimed.

Table IV combines MC statistical and systematic errors; Tables VI-VII provide systematic budgets. Rounded or censored table entries do not recover unrounded MC counts, weighting, shared nuisance covariance or the complete numerical integration. Equation 7 prints a product of individual rate densities without an explicit joint normalization; its implementation and boundary conventions must be resolved before replay. This is not evidence that the published numerical limits are erroneous.

The surviving muon-channel candidate is the earlier SK-IV upper-momentum conventional-volume candidate. A second earlier candidate moved outside the signal region after recalibration; changed selection does not create an independent acquisition.

claims.statement: Under the published Bayesian selection and nuisance model, the reported 90 percent lower bounds are tau/B(p -> e+ pi0)>2.4e34 years and tau/B(p -> mu+ pi0)>1.6e34 years.

limitations: The measured beam observable is a proton-producing decay rate relative to the monitored neutron population in the trapping region. Identifying its inverse with the total free-neutron lifetime requires the stated decay-channel and detection assumptions. Storage disappearance and proton counting are distinct observables; no branching fraction or explanation of their difference is inferred here.

Cancellation of the neutron velocity distribution assumes a thin monitor with inverse-velocity response and unchanged beam between the trap and monitor. Finite absorption, spatial profiles, scattering and beam transport still require the original corrections.

The effective trap length is L=n*l+L_end. A fit of the proton-to-monitor count-rate ratio versus electrode number removes a constant end contribution only under the common-end-region assumption; the paper separately corrects nonlinearity from field, geometry and beam divergence. Proton trapping for milliseconds is not neutron storage for a lifetime.

The neutron-lifetime results do not establish neutron formation, proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a present-day beam/bottle discrepancy. The 2013 historical world averages are not admitted without review of their components.
claims.scope: The Nico 2000-2001 proton-counting beam acquisition, its published 2005 lifetime and the Yue 2011 monitor calibration applied in 2013 to the same acquisition.
claims.statement: In the ideal corrected beam model, R_p=epsilon_p*N_n/tau and R_monitor=epsilon_0*v_0*N_n/L, so tau=L*epsilon_p*R_monitor/(epsilon_0*v_0*R_p). R_p counts detected proton-producing decays, and epsilon_0 is the monitor efficiency at the reference speed v_0.

limitations: Nico 2005 refines the earlier report of the June 2000-February 2001 acquisition. Yue 2013 applies a new monitor calibration completed in 2011 to that same acquisition. These publications are not independent neutron-lifetime replications and cannot be averaged as such.

The 2011 AlphaGamma calibration measures the same physical fluence monitor against an absolute neutron-rate transfer involving an absorbing 10B4C target, prompt gamma detectors and an alpha-source calibration chain. It removes evaluated 6Li cross-section and deposit-mass dependence from that monitor-calibration step, not all assumptions or corrections in the lifetime analysis. The raw absolute-calibration data and full correction covariance remain unreproduced.

Yue 2013 author manuscript v2 Equation 1 requires epsilon_0=epsilon_measured*lambda_0/lambda_mono. Equation 2 prints the opposite wavelength ratio, inconsistent with Equation 1 and its reported numerical value. The local conversion uses Equation 1 and preserves this author-version conflict; the publisher PDF was not reviewed and an error in the published numerical analysis is not established.

The calibration gives epsilon_measured=(8.5797+/-0.0048)e-5 at lambda_mono=0.49605+/-0.00012 nm; lambda_0=0.1798 nm corresponds to the stated 2200 m/s convention. The paper reports epsilon_0=(3.1098+/-0.0017)e-5, versus the previous calculated (3.1148+/-0.0094)e-5. These are monitor counting efficiencies, not neutron survival probabilities or unit charged-particle detection efficiencies.

Transfer of the 2011 efficiency to the earlier acquisition assumes temporal stability. New aperture metrology is attributed to improved measurement rather than physical change, with adopted DeltaOmega=0 and no added uncertainty. A three-hypothesis Bayesian deposit-loss comparison uses three foils, older activity data, Gaussian observations and a loss-only prior. The authors adopt DeltaRho=0 with 0.1 percent density uncertainty. These controls do not prove zero drift; the stability posterior and upstream measurements are not replayed.

The neutron-lifetime results do not establish neutron formation, proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a present-day beam/bottle discrepancy. The 2013 historical world averages are not admitted without review of their components.

limitations: The measured beam observable is a proton-producing decay rate relative to the monitored neutron population in the trapping region. Identifying its inverse with the total free-neutron lifetime requires the stated decay-channel and detection assumptions. Storage disappearance and proton counting are distinct observables; no branching fraction or explanation of their difference is inferred here.

Nico 2005 refines the earlier report of the June 2000-February 2001 acquisition. Yue 2013 applies a new monitor calibration completed in 2011 to that same acquisition. These publications are not independent neutron-lifetime replications and cannot be averaged as such.

Cancellation of the neutron velocity distribution assumes a thin monitor with inverse-velocity response and unchanged beam between the trap and monitor. Finite absorption, spatial profiles, scattering and beam transport still require the original corrections.

The acquisition counts released decay protons in an accelerated silicon-detector readout and alpha/triton products from the downstream 6LiF monitor. Live time, timing-dependent backgrounds, dead time, proton backscatter, dead-layer loss and neutron corrections remain part of the analysis. The selected count files, geometry simulation and SRIM loss extrapolation are not independently replayed.

The 2011 AlphaGamma calibration measures the same physical fluence monitor against an absolute neutron-rate transfer involving an absorbing 10B4C target, prompt gamma detectors and an alpha-source calibration chain. It removes evaluated 6Li cross-section and deposit-mass dependence from that monitor-calibration step, not all assumptions or corrections in the lifetime analysis. The raw absolute-calibration data and full correction covariance remain unreproduced.

Yue 2013 author manuscript v2 Equation 1 requires epsilon_0=epsilon_measured*lambda_0/lambda_mono. Equation 2 prints the opposite wavelength ratio, inconsistent with Equation 1 and its reported numerical value. The local conversion uses Equation 1 and preserves this author-version conflict; the publisher PDF was not reviewed and an error in the published numerical analysis is not established.

The calibration gives epsilon_measured=(8.5797+/-0.0048)e-5 at lambda_mono=0.49605+/-0.00012 nm; lambda_0=0.1798 nm corresponds to the stated 2200 m/s convention. The paper reports epsilon_0=(3.1098+/-0.0017)e-5, versus the previous calculated (3.1148+/-0.0094)e-5. These are monitor counting efficiencies, not neutron survival probabilities or unit charged-particle detection efficiencies.

Transfer of the 2011 efficiency to the earlier acquisition assumes temporal stability. New aperture metrology is attributed to improved measurement rather than physical change, with adopted DeltaOmega=0 and no added uncertainty. A three-hypothesis Bayesian deposit-loss comparison uses three foils, older activity data, Gaussian observations and a loss-only prior. The authors adopt DeltaRho=0 with 0.1 percent density uncertainty. These controls do not prove zero drift; the stability posterior and upstream measurements are not replayed.

Equation 4 rescales the old central lifetime by epsilon_0_old/epsilon_0_new and the adopted (1+DeltaOmega)*(1+DeltaRho) factors. Yue adds no proton-counting systematic correction beyond Nico 2005. Independence of the two neutron-fluence calibrations does not make the resulting lifetime estimates independent. The old full lifetime uncertainty and old efficiency must not be independently propagated as unrelated inputs.

The updated central lifetime is reported as 887.7 seconds, with 1.2 statistical and 1.9 systematic seconds in the abstract and 2.3 seconds total in the body and Table II. The displayed five-component budget and abstract split contain rounded values. Their central quadratures do not reconstruct unrounded errors or shared covariance, and their small rounding differences do not establish an error.

The neutron-lifetime results do not establish neutron formation, proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a present-day beam/bottle discrepancy. The 2013 historical world averages are not admitted without review of their components.

limitations: Baryon number and net flavor are additive sector labels in the stated strong-interaction description. They do not specify a total quark, antiquark or gluon population, sector probabilities, a free-particle census or weak-decay stability.

The three-factor minimum concerns nonempty tensor powers of the fundamental color representation without antiquarks or adjoint factors. It is not a minimum for arbitrary color representations, every hadron, or a graph construction rule. Color SU(3) and approximate flavor SU(3) are distinct.

The Fock expansion is a representation with specified quantization, gauge, regulator and renormalization conventions. No coefficient, Hamiltonian eigenstate, parton distribution, mass, magnetic response or formation trajectory is computed here.
The executable establishes exact algebra under declared definitions. It neither proves confinement nor shows that a color-invariant tensor is a dynamically realized or stable physical particle.
claims.scope: Declared QCD occupation-basis labels, additive flavor charges and fundamental color representations; no empirical constituent census or bound-state solution.
claims.statement: In the declared strong-interaction nucleon sectors, net flavor means quarks minus antiquarks: proton (N_u,N_d)=(2,1), neutron (1,2), with zero other net flavors. With B=sum_f N_f/3 and Q/e=sum_f q_f*N_f, these labels give B=1 and charges +1 and 0. Adding a same-flavor quark-antiquark pair or gluons preserves these additive labels without preserving total basis-particle count.

claims.scope: Selected light-flavor meson classification and KLOE 2001-2002 radiative ratio with conditional mixing; no universal formation claim.
claims.statement: The flavor-octet and singlet isoscalar basis vectors are (|u ubar>+|d dbar>-2|s sbar>)/sqrt(6) and (|u ubar>+|d dbar>+|s sbar>)/sqrt(3). Physical eta and eta-prime are rotated combinations, not exact octet/singlet labels. In the restricted flavor basis |eta>=cos(phi_P)*|q qbar>-sin(phi_P)*|s sbar> and |eta-prime>=sin(phi_P)*|q qbar>+cos(phi_P)*|s sbar>, with |q qbar>=(|u ubar>+|d dbar>)/sqrt(2) and theta_P=phi_P-arctan(sqrt(2)). Each ket labels a quark-antiquark basis state, not a subtraction or a complete observed particle population.

limitations: The reported fit uses 70 particle-type, momentum and zenith bins, weighted Monte Carlo statistics and nuisance penalties from Equations 2-4 and Table II. Overall normalization alpha floats freely despite an estimated 25% prior uncertainty; it is not included as a 25% Gaussian constraint. The v2 multi-GeV FC mu-like weight contains (1-rho*N_PC/(2*N_mu)), whereas PC has (1+rho/2). Neither weights, response, minimization, contour coverage nor significance are locally reconstructed.

The physical best fit has sin^2(2 theta)=1 and Delta m^2=2.2e-3 eV^2; the unconstrained minimum at sin^2(2 theta)=1.05 lies outside the physical region. Reported confidence contours are referenced to the physical minimum with the authors' bounded-region prescription, not generic two-parameter thresholds supplied locally. This is a historical effective two-flavor mass-squared difference, not an absolute mass, a modern three-flavor global fit or a mass-generation mechanism.

The source explicitly says this sample cannot distinguish nu_mu-to-nu_tau from disappearance into a non-interacting sterile species; it does not directly observe tau appearance. Its separate nu_mu-to-nu_e comparison includes Earth matter effects and is disfavored within the tested model, not an exclusion of every alternative theory.

citations.note: Supports the selected formal convention and its stated model limits; no experimental inference is admitted by this definition.

limitations: Use a closed unitary three-active-neutrino model with standard weak interactions, hbar=c=1 and fixed positive energy in the ultrarelativistic coherent forward-scattering approximation. The prescribed medium is electrically neutral, unpolarized and locally isotropic, with nonrelativistic electrons, protons and neutrons and no appreciable muon/tau population. Incoherent scattering, absorption, neutrino-neutrino refraction, sterile states and nonstandard interactions require different models.

The vector f contains flavor amplitudes, with the already declared U_alpha,i convention. The review writes its basic evolution equation in the vacuum mass basis; multiplication by the constant U gives the stated flavor-basis Hamiltonian. For antineutrinos both U becomes U* and the charged-current potential changes sign. A merely diagonal potential cannot in general be discarded; the neutral-current term is removable here because it is common to all three active flavors.

Vacuum masses, the mixing matrix, energy and the medium density profile are supplied inputs. Matter-dependent eigenvalues are effective propagation parameters, not newly generated vacuum masses. This model does not determine absolute mass, Dirac/Majorana nature, an origin mechanism, universal carrier minima or a temporal emergence order.

A variable density generally gives noncommuting Hamiltonians at different positions. Its evolution requires the ordered solution with initial conditions; one cannot substitute a single constant-density vacuum phase or assume adiabaticity from an instantaneous mixing angle. No actual solar/Earth profile, scattering experiment, oscillation fit or matter evolution is numerically reproduced here.
claims.scope: Formal coherent propagation in a prescribed ordinary medium and its stated two-flavor approximation; no empirical mass-generation or solar-fit claim.
claims.statement: For flavor amplitudes f, i*df/dx=H_f(x)*f with H_f=U diag(m_i^2) U-dagger/(2E)+diag(V_e(x),0,0), after removing a common identity term. For neutrinos V_e=sqrt(2)*G_F*n_e(x); for antineutrinos U is complex-conjugated and V_e changes sign. For neutrinos in neutral ordinary matter the active-sector neutral-current contribution is -G_F*n_n(x)/sqrt(2) times the identity and changes only a common phase; its sign also reverses for antineutrinos before removal.

claims.statement: In the declared two-flavor approximation set A=2E*(V_e-V_x) and Delta_m=sqrt[(Delta*cos(2 theta)-A)^2+(Delta*sin(2 theta))^2]. limitations: Equation 1 uses independent channel Poisson factors and Gaussian background nuisance terms as the authors' statistical model. The rounded table does not fully specify nuisance domains, unrounded inputs or pseudoexperiment construction. Neither the likelihood, significance calibration nor confidence coverage is locally reproduced.

The Fisher product of channel tail probabilities is a test statistic, not the final calibrated p value. A total-count Poisson tail with background mean 0.25 is not the reported channel-aware 1.1e-7 result. Significance is a background-hypothesis tail comparison, not a posterior probability that oscillations are true.

The reported 2.64 +/-0.53 expected signal adopts Delta m23^2=2.44e-3 eV^2 and sin^2(2 theta23)=1. Its quoted uncertainty includes model and efficiency inputs. These nominal parameters are not independently determined by the expectation and are not retroactively replaced by the fitted interval.

The signal-strength errors are a 90% confidence interval, not one-standard-deviation errors. The mass-squared result additionally assumes full mixing and reuses the selected data/model. It is not an absolute mass, a complete three-flavor global fit, a Dirac/Majorana test or a unique mass-generation mechanism.

Earlier OPERA candidate publications use subsets of this same 2008–2012 exposure. The fifth event contributes to the four-channel total; candidate displays, significance, strength and mass-squared interval are dependent results. The two statistical implementations are not independent experiments.

limitations: The selected beam passage quotes contamination in terms of interactions, not incident flux fractions: antimuon neutrinos 2.1%, electron plus antielectron neutrinos below 1%, intrinsic tau-neutrino component of order 1e-6. These are adopted beam-composition conditions. The approximately 17 GeV mean is not each event energy.

Equation 1 uses independent channel Poisson factors and Gaussian background nuisance terms as the authors' statistical model. The rounded table does not fully specify nuisance domains, unrounded inputs or pseudoexperiment construction. Neither the likelihood, significance calibration nor confidence coverage is locally reproduced.

The Fisher product of channel tail probabilities is a test statistic, not the final calibrated p value. A total-count Poisson tail with background mean 0.25 is not the reported channel-aware 1.1e-7 result. Significance is a background-hypothesis tail comparison, not a posterior probability that oscillations are true.

Earlier OPERA candidate publications use subsets of this same 2008–2012 exposure. The fifth event contributes to the four-channel total; candidate displays, significance, strength and mass-squared interval are dependent results. The two statistical implementations are not independent experiments.

These source-specific appearance results supply no universal carrier minimum, weighted parent necessity, temporal emergence ordering or SOMA property/level validation. They do not by themselves establish astrophysical transport or cosmological predictions.

claims.statement: For two effectively massless physical daughter four-momenta from a two-body decay, define mT^2 = 2 pT1 pT2 (1-cos(deltaPhi)); the exact parent invariant mass then obeys M >= mT. Replacing these quantities by reconstructed electron and missing transverse vectors defines an estimator under a single-invisible-daughter assignment. Response errors can make that estimator exceed the true mass, so the exact inequality is not an eventwise detector guarantee. The transverse recoil is the magnitude of the daughter transverse-vector sum; mT is not a fully reconstructed invariant mass.

limitations: A criterion must declare the gauge theory, dynamical matter, state or temperature regime, operator, separation/time limits and regulator. Pure-gauge fundamental Wilson-loop area law, screened static-source energies with dynamical quarks and phenomenological color-singlet final states are not interchangeable definitions.

The area-law criterion takes large contours and static-source limits in an unscreened theory. Wilson strong-coupling surfaces and Creutz finite SU(2) loops do not prove continuum SU(3) confinement with physical quark masses. Their finite-volume, finite-loop and extrapolation restrictions remain explicit.

Pair creation in the reviewed dynamical-quark calculations permits color-singlet static-light or static-strange channels. The screened ground-state energy need not grow indefinitely with separation. A metastable string branch, an operator overlap and the true ground state are different quantities; Euclidean mixing energies do not measure real-time hadronization rates.

Source card 1.31 supplies possible nonperturbative formulations, including a chosen lattice action and operator basis; it is not an observed universal organization stage. Source card 1.30 supplies a renormalization prescription and scale, not physical elapsed time or a demonstrated temporal maintenance cause. Source card 1.3 supplies the non-Abelian gluon sector within QCD, not an independently measured universal maintenance arrow.

The original parent weights 0.55, 0.20 and 0.25, N_min=N_crit=1 elementary-particle counts, necessary-parent labels, TypeRole/SOMA phase placement and macro-to-micro causal story are unsupported. They have no active scientific semantics. Classification as a regime-level pattern is descriptive, not a verified universal phase sequence or material carrier.
The excluded universal downward constraint from source card 1.15 remains excluded. No intervention, closed effective dynamics or universal generating rule is established by the static-source results.

Electrical fractional-charge bounds constrain a declared material or particle search. Electric charge is not color charge; a null result cannot establish absence of all free colored objects. In particular, the CMS fractional-charge benchmark explicitly uses color-singlet particles.

Color-singlet tensor algebra is a representation constraint, not a dynamical formation proof. Asymptotic freedom concerns ultraviolet running and does not prove the infrared criterion. The high-temperature phase diagram, physical-point continuum completion and a mathematical all-channel confinement theorem are outside this admission.

No universal nuclear or atomic stability follows from the definition or the selected hadron results. Nuclear binding, decay channels and electromagnetic atomic binding require distinct systems and inputs; the existing deuteron beta threshold excludes one specified bare-nucleus breakup channel, not all decays, nuclei or atomic states.

The QCD interpretation of hadronic final states is a separate phenomenological statement, not an equivalent finite-loop test or a proof that separation energy grows without bound.

The averaged survival is <P_ee>_s=integral dE w_s(E) integral d^3r f_s(r|E) P_ee(E,r). For a specified electron-flavor charged-current response, w_s is proportional to the unoscillated differential neutrino number flux dPhi_s/dE at the detector times its cross section and detection efficiency, with any selected-bin response included and the finite nonzero normalization divided out. Here dPhi_s/dE counts neutrinos per unit area, time and neutrino energy; the transported energy flux E*dPhi_s/dE would introduce an extra energy factor and is not the event weight.

limitations: Use the closed unitary active two- or three-state convention already declared. Oscillatory flavor probabilities require both mixing of contributing components and nonzero relative mass-squared differences, together with the stated production/detection and propagation coherence conditions. A degenerate pair, unmixed channel or suppressed interference need not show an oscillatory signal.

A single vacuum mass eigenstate acquires only a phase in its internal state; its flavor-readout probabilities |U_alpha,i|^2 do not oscillate. An incoherent density matrix diagonal in the vacuum mass basis also has constant vacuum flavor probabilities. These are not statements that vacuum mass states remain instantaneous eigenstates in arbitrary varying matter, or that packet position is stationary.

Leptonic charged-current flavor labels specify preparation/readout; mass differences and mixing specify model inputs. They do not establish necessary physical parents, an arising chronology, weights 0.3/0.7, N_min=N_crit=1, a SOMA phase/type or the claim that flavor identity can never be dynamically autonomous. No causal maintenance or downward constraint is inferred from these definition dependencies.

Within this oscillation model, mass-squared differences constrain differences only. They do not determine the absolute mass scale, require every individual mass to be nonzero, select Dirac versus Majorana character or supply a unique mass-generation extension. Mass origin remains a separate scope.

Continuous weak scattering or repeated projective collapse is not the coherent phase mechanism. A specified source, medium and detector determine which probability or weighted response is appropriate; transport and cosmological claims need additional inputs.
claims.scope: Flavor preparation/readout and conditional coherent propagation; no universal ontological class, formation order or mass-origin inference.
claims.statement: In the declared coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model, flavor-sensitive preparation and readout are related by interference between distinct mass propagation components. Their relative phases change transition probabilities as L/E varies; a probability is not a continuously measured sequence of flavor jumps. Oscillation is a conditional propagation phenomenon, not an additional bounded object or a universal property of every neutrino state.

limitations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. Each chain retains its acquisition, selection, adopted flux/cross sections, detector response, backgrounds and inference contexts. Counts are not event-level oscillation probabilities. Reused events, multiple summaries and alternative fits within an acquisition are dependent; this synthesis is not another independent experiment or combined significance.

KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

limitations: The supplied 3-by-3 unitary model is distinct from a general 3-by-n charged-current matrix or an effective light-sector submatrix after heavy states are removed. The latter need not be exactly unitary; this definition does not establish that extra states are absent.

The phase count assumes generic nondegenerate nonzero masses. Degenerate masses, a massless state or vanishing mixing angles can remove phases or their observable effects. A nontrivial mixing matrix need not violate CP, and a complex entry alone is not a rephasing-invariant measurement.

For the same ordinary vacuum channel, U_prime(alpha,i)=exp(i r_alpha) U(alpha,i) exp(i c_i) gives A_prime(alpha,beta)=exp(i(r_beta-r_alpha)) A(alpha,beta), so its probability is unchanged. This column-phase invariance of the oscillation amplitude does not permit arbitrary rephasing of a Majorana field at fixed real mass in the full Lagrangian.

Majorana column-phase cancellation concerns ordinary lepton-number-conserving oscillations. It does not make those phases unphysical in all processes or identify neutrinos as Dirac or Majorana. The chosen angles, phases and conventions supply no fitted parameter values or current ordering preference.
claims.scope: A declared PMNS convention and phase-counting boundary; not measured angle values, CP violation or a determination of neutrino mass character.
claims.statement: In a supplied closed unitary three-active-neutrino model, define U=R23 R13(delta) R12 P. Each real ij rotation acts on its plane with block [[cij,sij],[-sij,cij]] and as identity on the remaining direction, with cij=cos(thetaij) and sij=sin(thetaij); the 1-3 block is [[c13,s13 exp(-i delta)],[-s13 exp(i delta),c13]]. For generic three-mass mixing, charged-lepton and Dirac-neutrino rephasings leave three angles and one Dirac phase, with P=I. In the Majorana alternative use P=diag(exp(i eta1),exp(i eta2),1); these two extra column phases cancel from ordinary mass-induced flavor-oscillation probabilities.

limitations: The massless statement uses the minimal renormalizable field content and its accidental symmetries. It is not a prohibition on all gauge-invariant Standard Model effective operators: the stated dimension-five extension changes that assumption.

claims.statement: With the usual fermion content, one Higgs doublet and no right-handed neutrino singlets, the minimal renormalizable Standard Model has no neutrino Dirac Yukawa term and leaves neutrinos massless. Formal extensions can add singlet neutrinos and Dirac masses, with total lepton number imposed to exclude Majorana terms, or allow lepton-number-violating Majorana masses. A dimension-five operator built from the lepton and Higgs doublets can instead generate a Majorana mass after electroweak symmetry breaking. These are alternative model constructions; flavor-oscillation evidence alone does not select one.

citations.note: The leading vacuum phase and squared-mass-difference dependence support this explicit algebraic consequence; the conditional positivity argument and counterexamples are stated here, not reported as new empirical results.

limitations: This is a conditional algebraic consequence of the declared leading vacuum phase, not a new measurement, global fit or independent replication of mass splittings. Fixed preparation, energy and detector response are assumed; endpoint kinematics, time of flight, coherence conditions and higher-order dispersion are not covered by this invariance.

An admissible common shift changes the absolute mass scale without changing these probabilities. No unique absolute masses, measured upper bound, mass ordering, Dirac versus Majorana character or mass-generation mechanism follows from this statement. Keeping the ultrarelativistic approximation valid is not an experimentally inferred upper bound.

Two nonzero differences alone are insufficient: (m_1^2,m_2^2,m_3^2)=(q,0,0), q>0, gives Delta21=Delta31=-q and only one nonzero mass. The unequal-differences condition excludes this degeneracy. Conversely (0,a,b), with a,b>0 and a!=b, meets the condition while one mass is zero; all three need not be nonzero.

The three-state and nonnegative-mass assumptions are explicit. Separate historical effective two-flavor fits are not automatically a joint closed three-state likelihood; their best-fit numbers are not identified here with exact three-state splittings or pooled into new constraints.
claims.scope: Formal identifiability of squared-mass differences in a supplied leading three-state vacuum oscillation model.
claims.statement: In the leading coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum model with hbar=c=1, hold U, L and E fixed. Replacing every m_i^2 by m_i^2+kappa multiplies A_alpha-to-beta by exp[-i kappa L/(2E)], leaving P=|A|^2 unchanged. This holds for shifts preserving m_i^2+kappa>=0 and (m_i^2+kappa)/E^2<<1. For three nonnegative squared masses, Delta21=m_2^2-m_1^2 and Delta31=m_3^2-m_1^2 both nonzero and unequal imply three pairwise distinct values; at most one can be zero, so at least two masses are nonzero.

The selected color-sensitive and weak-channel results are compatible with specified predictions, not direct observation of a universal sector-differentiation event or a proof of every field representation, gauge-group global form, generation, coupling or particle lineage. Other species and decay studies retain their existing scopes; generic collider/scattering placeholders do not admit unreviewed data.

The gauge/matter/Higgs decomposition is a declared model input. A general QFT framework, a chosen Hamiltonian and electroweak symmetry breaking do not dynamically derive that content or establish the original necessary/enabling parents, 0.6/0.4 weights, Nmin=Ncrit=1, temporal arising/maintenance or SOMA pattern authority. Distinct gauge factors do not imply isolated physical sectors.
